subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number (n = 0 is allowed) and let kappa > 0 and omega > 0 be real numbers. Then there exist real numbers delta_P and C_P (depending only on n, kappa and omega) with 0 < delta_P, delta_P <= 1/8, delta_P <= kappa, 0 < C_P and C_P * delta_P <= 1/2, such that for every real t with 0 < t <= delta_P, writing Lambda := t/kappa and q := (1 + t)/(1 - 3t)^n (natural-number power), the following three inequalities hold: (a) e^(2 Lambda) * (q * omega) + 2 * e^Lambda * Lambda <= (1 + C_P t) * omega; (b) (1 - C_P t) * omega <= e^(-Lambda) * (omega - Lambda); (c) e^Lambda * (e^Lambda * (q * omega) + Lambda - omega) <= C_P * omega * t.

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (choice of delta_P and C_P through the C^1 functions g_+, g_-, g_c and the mean value theorem), with kappa = (p-n)/(4p) and omega_n replaced by arbitrary kappa > 0 and omega > 0 and the three bounds multiplied by omega (G_+ = omega g_+, G_- = omega g_-, G_c = omega g_c). The parent applies the result with kappa = (p-n)/(4p) and omega = unitBallVolume n, before the codimension l is chosen.

Notation. Fix n, kappa > 0, omega > 0. Let I be the open interval (-1/24, 1/4); for t in I we have 1 - 3t > 1/4 > 0. For t in I put Lambda(t) := t/kappa, q(t) := (1 + t)/(1 - 3t)^n, and
 G_+(t) := e^(2 Lambda(t)) (q(t) omega) + 2 e^(Lambda(t)) Lambda(t),
 G_-(t) := e^(-Lambda(t)) (omega - Lambda(t)),
 G_c(t) := e^(Lambda(t)) (e^(Lambda(t)) (q(t) omega) + Lambda(t) - omega).

1. Smoothness. t -> Lambda(t) is linear, exp is C^infinity, t -> 1 + t is a polynomial and t -> (1 - 3t)^n is a polynomial with no zero on I, so q = (1 + t) ((1 - 3t)^n)^(-1) is C^infinity on I. Hence G_+, G_-, G_c, which are sums and products of these functions, are C^infinity (in particular C^1) on I. Explicitly, with Lambda = Lambda(t), q = q(t):
 q'(t) = (1 - 3t)^(-n) + 3n (1 + t)(1 - 3t)^(-n-1),
 G_+'(t) = (2/kappa) e^(2 Lambda) q omega + e^(2 Lambda) q'(t) omega + (2/kappa) e^Lambda (Lambda + 1),
 G_-'(t) = -(1/kappa) e^(-Lambda) (omega - Lambda + 1),
 G_c'(t) = (1/kappa) e^Lambda (e^Lambda q omega + Lambda - omega) + e^Lambda ((1/kappa) e^Lambda q omega + e^Lambda q'(t) omega + 1/kappa);
all of these are continuous on I.

subproblems.title: Density at least 1 at support points inside the open ball B°_rho(0) under 2.3 (Simon Ch. 4, 4.9-4.10(1))
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1 and l >= 0 be natural numbers, p > n a real number, kappa := (p - n)/(4p), U an open subset of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U (RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu := V.weight, H : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), and delta, rho real numbers with 0 < delta <= kappa such that the hypotheses 2.3 hold (V.AllardHypotheses H p delta rho). Assume moreover (T0) x -> V.tangentProj x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (T1) for mu-a.e. x, V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection for some n-dimensional subspace P; (T3) for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x). Then for every y in spt V cap B°_rho(0) (spt V = V.support = U cap spt mu; B°_rho(0) the open ball) and every real t with V.HasDensity y t (i.e. mu(B_r(y))/ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal t as r -> 0+, closed balls, omega_n = unitBallVolume n), we have 1 <= t. In words: Theta^n(mu, y) >= 1 at every point y of spt V inside the open ball B°_rho(0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ (p - n) / (4 * p) → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x)) → ∀ y ∈ V.support ∩ ball (0 : Amb n ℓ) ρ, ∀ t : ℝ, V.HasDensity y t → 1 ≤ t
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 4, 4.9 and 4.10(1): upper semicontinuity of the density and Theta >= 1 on spt V), with the monotonicity facts (M) supplied by the sibling annular_monotonicity and the curvature scaling of step 2 supplied by the sibling subball_bounds.

Notation. mu := V.weight; B_r(z) closed balls, B°_r(z) open balls; kappa := (p - n)/(4p) > 0; alpha' := 1 - n/p in (0, 1); omega_n := unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2 + 1) > 0; W := B°_rho(0); Lambda := delta/kappa, so 0 < Lambda <= 1 (from 0 < delta <= kappa) and kappa Lambda = delta. From V.AllardHypotheses H p delta rho we use rho > 0, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H, V.mult >= 1 mu-a.e., and mu(B_rho(0)) <= ofReal((1 + delta) omega_n rho^n) < infinity.

1. Uniqueness of densities. If V.HasDensity x t and V.HasDensity x t', then ofReal t = ofReal t', because both are limits of the same function along the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 in R, which is not trivial, in the Hausdorff space [0, infinity]. Hence t = t' whenever t, t' >= 0; and if t' > 0 then t = t' (ofReal t = t' > 0 forces t > 0).

2. Monotonicity at the points of W. Let x in W and 0 < R' <= rho - |x|. Then R' <= rho and B_(R')(x) is contained in B_rho(0) (|z| <= |x| + R' <= rho). By subball_bounds (with z := x, r := R'), B_(R')(x) is contained in U and V.scaledLpNorm H p x R' <= ofReal delta = ofReal(kappa Lambda). (T1) implies its local form (for mu-a.e. x', if x' in B°_(R')(x) then V.tangentProj x' is the projection onto an n-dimensional subspace), and (T0) implies a.e.-strong measurability of x' -> V.tangentProj x' for mu restricted to B°_(R')(x). Hence annular_monotonicity applies with centre x, radius R' and this Lambda: there are F : R -> R and t_(x,R') >= 0 such that, for every r in (0, R'), F(r) >= e^(-Lambda) > 0 and |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R')^(alpha'), V.HasDensity x t_(x,R'), and omega_n t_(x,R') <= F(r) r^(-n) mu(B_r(x)).toReal + F(r) - 1 for every r in (0, R'). Define Theta(x) := t_(x, rho - |x|) >= 0, so V.HasDensity x Theta(x); by step 1, t_(x,R') = Theta(x) for every admissible R'. With c := Lambda (r/R')^(alpha') we have F(r) <= 1 + c, F(r) - 1 <= c and mu(B_r(x)).toReal >= 0, hence
 (2.1) omega_n Theta(x) <= (1 + Lambda (r/R')^(alpha')) r^(-n) mu(B_r(x)).toReal + Lambda (r/R')^(alpha') for all x in W, 0 < R' <= rho - |x| and 0 < r < R'.

3. Upper semicontinuity of Theta on W. Let x in W and eta > 0. Put R_0 := (rho - |x|)/3 > 0 and c(r) := Lambda (r/R_0)^(alpha') for r > 0; c(r) -> 0 as r -> 0+ because alpha' > 0.
 (a) For 0 < r <= 3 R_0 = rho - |x|, mu(B_r(x)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) < infinity, so mu(B_r(x))/ofReal(omega_n r^n) = ofReal(mu(B_r(x)).toReal/(omega_n r^n)). Since V.HasDensity x Theta(x) and toReal is continuous at the finite value ofReal Theta(x), r^(-n) mu(B_r(x)).toReal -> omega_n Theta(x) as r -> 0+. Choose r in (0, R_0) with (1 + c(r)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(x)).toReal + c(r) < omega_n Theta(x) + omega_n eta/2.
 (b) The closed balls B_(r')(x), r' in (r, 3R_0], have finite measure and decrease to their intersection B_r(x) as r' decreases to r, so mu(B_(r')(x)) -> mu(B_r(x)) (continuity from above). Choose r' in (r, 2 R_0) with (1 + c(r)) r^(-n) mu(B_(r')(x)).toReal + c(r) < omega_n Theta(x) + omega_n eta.
 (c) Put d := min{R_0, r' - r} > 0 and let x' in B°_d(x). Then |x'| < |x| + R_0 < rho, so x' in W, and rho - |x'| > rho - |x| - R_0 = 2 R_0 >= R_0; moreover B_r(x') is contained in B_(r')(x), because |z - x| <= |z - x'| + |x' - x| < r + d <= r'. By (2.1) at x' with R' := R_0 and this r < R_0, and monotonicity of mu (all masses finite),
 omega_n Theta(x') <= (1 + c(r)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(x')).toReal + c(r) <= (1 + c(r)) r^(-n) mu(B_(r')(x)).toReal + c(r) < omega_n Theta(x) + omega_n eta.
 Hence B°_d(x) is contained in W and Theta(x') < Theta(x) + eta for every x' in B°_d(x).

4. Theta >= 1 almost everywhere on W. By (T3) and V.mult >= 1 mu-a.e. (from 2.3), for mu-a.e. x we have V.HasDensity x (V.mult x) and V.mult x >= 1. For such x in W, step 1 (with t' := V.mult x > 0) gives Theta(x) = V.mult x >= 1. Thus for mu-a.e. x: if x in W then Theta(x) >= 1.

5. Conclusion. Let y in spt V cap W and t real with V.HasDensity y t. Suppose Theta(y) < 1. Step 3 with eta := (1 - Theta(y))/2 > 0 gives d > 0 with B°_d(y) contained in W and Theta(x') < 1 for all x' in B°_d(y). By step 4, mu-a.e. x satisfies x not in B°_d(y), i.e. mu(B°_d(y)) = 0. But y in V.support is contained in spt mu, so every open neighbourhood of y, in particular B°_d(y), has positive mu-measure: a contradiction. Therefore Theta(y) >= 1 > 0, and step 1 (V.HasDensity y t and V.HasDensity y Theta(y)) gives t = Theta(y) >= 1.

1. Preliminaries. For r in (0, R), (H1) gives mu(B_r) <= ofReal M < infinity, hence mu(B_r) = ofReal(m(r)) and 0 <= m(r) <= M (as M >= 0). By (H2), F(r) >= e^(-Lambda) > 0, F(r) <= e^Lambda, F(r) - 1 <= Lambda and 1 - F(r) <= Lambda.

2. Upper bound for Phi. For r in (0, R), Phi(r) <= e^Lambda r^(-n) M + Lambda, because 0 <= F(r) <= e^Lambda, 0 <= r^(-n) m(r) <= r^(-n) M and F(r) - 1 <= Lambda. Fix s in (0, R). For every r in [s, R), (H3) gives Phi(s) <= Phi(r) <= e^Lambda r^(-n) M + Lambda. The map r -> e^Lambda r^(-n) M + Lambda is continuous at R > 0, so letting r -> R from the left:
 (dagger) Phi(s) <= e^Lambda (M/R^n) + Lambda.

3. (i). By (dagger) and 1 - F(s) <= Lambda, F(s) s^(-n) m(s) = Phi(s) + 1 - F(s) <= e^Lambda (M/R^n) + 2 Lambda. The right side is >= 0 and F(s) >= e^(-Lambda) > 0, hence s^(-n) m(s) <= (e^Lambda (M/R^n) + 2 Lambda)/F(s) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda (M/R^n) + 2 Lambda) = e^(2 Lambda)(M/R^n) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda. Multiplying by s^n > 0 gives m(s) <= (e^(2 Lambda)(M/R^n) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda) s^n, so mu(B_s) = ofReal(m(s)) <= ofReal((e^(2 Lambda)(M/R^n) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda) s^n) by monotonicity of ofReal.

4. (ii). Assume (H4). Then omega <= Phi(s) = F(s) s^(-n) m(s) + F(s) - 1 <= F(s) s^(-n) m(s) + Lambda, so omega - Lambda <= F(s) s^(-n) m(s) <= e^Lambda s^(-n) m(s) (as s^(-n) m(s) >= 0 and F(s) <= e^Lambda). Multiplying by e^(-Lambda) > 0 and by s^n > 0: e^(-Lambda)(omega - Lambda) s^n <= m(s). Hence ofReal(e^(-Lambda)(omega - Lambda) s^n) <= ofReal(m(s)) = mu(B_s).

5. (iii). Assume (H4). For t in (0, s), (H3) applied to the pair (t, s) (0 < t <= s < R), (H4) at t, (dagger) and e^Lambda > 0 give
 integral^-_{B_s minus B_t} ofReal(g) dmu <= ofReal(e^Lambda (Phi(s) - Phi(t))) <= ofReal(e^Lambda (e^Lambda (M/R^n) + Lambda - omega)) =: Q,

The sets A_k := B_s minus B_(s/(k+2)) (k = 0, 1, 2, ...) increase with k, and their union is B_s minus {y}: if x in B_s and x != y then |x - y| > s/(k+2) for k large, while y lies in no A_k. For an increasing (hence directed) countable family of sets, the lower integral over the union equals the supremum of the lower integrals over the members, for an arbitrary [0, infinity]-valued integrand (Mathlib: setLIntegral_iUnion_of_directed); as s/(k+2) is in (0, s), each of these is <= Q, so integral^-_{B_s minus {y}} ofReal(g) dmu <= Q. Finally B_s is contained in (B_s minus {y}) union {y}, so by monotonicity and subadditivity of the lower integral in the domain (lintegral_union_le), and since integral^-_{{y}} ofReal(g) dmu = ofReal(g(y)) mu({y}) = 0 * mu({y}) = 0 (g(y) = 0, and 0 * infinity = 0 in [0, infinity]), we get integral^-_{B_s} ofReal(g) dmu <= Q.

6. Steps 3-5 prove (i), and under (H4) also (ii) and (iii), for every s in (0, R).
